questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Personal connection to the destination (heritage / friends there/ etc.)

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Paris is the city of all cities. With its unique architecture, culture, language and cuisine, Paris is the place to be in your 20's. And getting the possibility to experience Paris, for not just a week of vacation, but for half a year was something I couldn't pass up on. Further, Sorbonne is a unique institution deeply integrated into the Parisian and French history and getting the chance to study in the iconic buildings on Place de la Sorbonne and Rue du Panthéon is truly a once-in-a-lifetime opportunity. Also, the courses looked really interesting.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer:
Not that easy unfortunately. One important thing when going to Sorbonne (and other french universities, I could imagine) is that you need to have a lot of patience. And the information I got about the courses available turned out to be different from the final courses offered, meaning I had to change my learning agreement and chosen courses at the last minute. I would recommend to email
IRO.EES
@
univ-paris1.fr
if you have any questions and as quickly as possible, Chloe has been the most helpful in the process.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I was offered a one-week French course at Sorbonne in the introduction week, this was really helpful to connect with other students. There was also a an introduction meeting for all exchange students but this was held in French meaning many students were excluded from the information despite the invitation to the meeting being in English.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
You can find Sorbonne's housing assistance on their website, I didn't end up using this myself. 

I found housing through Fondation Danoise, the danish student house in the Cité Universitaire placed down in the 14th arr. The Cité consists of a wide range of country residences housing international students from all over the world, ranging from Swedish to Mexican students. Rent is relatively cheap compared to the rest of Paris 4000-5000 DKK. 

I would also recommend using the Danish facebook groups for Danes in Paris, like Padam Padam. Make a post or check regularly for new opportunities.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer:
There is no on/off campus living, Cité probably is the closest thing to campus living though. 

However, I would recommend living closer to the city centre if possible just for the sheer experience of doing so. The experiences I have had when staying in friends' apartments in the city centre have been truly amazing, like having a french balcony. Looking back today I would gladly had spent an extra 1000-2000 DKK a month to stay closer to the centre or in the north, like 10th, 11th, 19th or 20th arr.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer:
This process was maybe the worst thing about my stay in Paris. Three days prior to the courses starting, it had not been possible to sign up for any courses and we had no information on how to do so either. Finally, the economic department called us in to give us the information two days before the courses beginning. Upon registering for the courses, the available courses had changed so I had to make up a new course list on the spot while also being in a hurry due to the courses being first come first served. 

Also... when I showed up to the first class of one of my courses, we sat in crowded auditorium with nearly 100 students for one hour with no teacher, suddenly we received and email explaining that the course had been cancelled for the whole semester, they just forgot to tell us. Total scandal, I had to choose yet another course. But ultimately, it all worked out and the student councillors were helpful with changing courses.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer:
Very little help, mainly one student councillor called Chloe Hubbard,
IRO.EES
@
univ-paris1.fr
.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Not very succesful. I ended up taking 5 courses with only 2 being the ones I originally planned on taking.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be very patient. In the end it will all work out. Even though you will be frustrated, at least you're frustrated in Paris.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I ended up taking 2 master courses and 3 bachelor courses.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The biggest difference between Sorbonne and UCPH is the mandatory attendance. You have to present for all teaching exercises at Sorbonne. Also another thing is the grading, while at UCPH your grade consists 100% of your final test score, at Sorbonne in many courses the grade is divided into many parts. FX in one course 50% was the final grade, 20% was midterm 1, 20% was midterm 2 and 10% was attendance and participation.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
International Monetary Economics
Macroeconomics: Growth
Game Theory
Resources and Climate Change
Comparative Politics

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
I would recommend International Monetary Economics, it gives you a very cool deep dive into the monetary side of economics that we sometimes lack at UCPH. I would also recommend Resources and Climate Change if you're into climate economics. 

I would recommend against taking Game Theory as despite the course being presented as being in English, the teacher prefers speaking french...

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Good wine is way cheaper than in Denmark, take advantage of this. Also get a bike, Swapfiets has worked for me.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
Sport activities were available to students but often colliding with school activities. 

Sorbonne didn't really arrange anything social compared to other universities. Every activity between students was arranged by ourselves.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Just enjoy the city.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Just take advantage of being in Paris. Try and avoid the most touristy areas, instead go spend time where the Parisians spend time. Go to Belleville, go to Rue du Faubourg Saint-Denis, go to jazz clubs, go to canal st martin. Try and explore the 10th, 11th, 19th and 20th as much as possible.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer:
Relatively easy. Most importantly, learn some French. Remember to say bonjour, merci, s'il vous plait. Embrace the culture you're living in and try to be a part of it. And go to as many boulangeries as possible and find the best croissant, pain au chocolat and sandwich. 

Also read A Moveable Feast by Hemingway.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: This is the hardest part, try and be active in the teaching exercises or go to Rue Mouffetard in the weekends or after class, here you will often find a lot of students from Sorbonne.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The language and tonality.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The joy of life and slow tempo of life.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Be open to new people and new experiences
2. Don't hold back
3. Live the parisian life you've always dreamt of

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: No

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting so many amazing people and sharing amazing memories together.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Leaving home but also leaving Paris.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
